task_text: Lever launch, catch and reload: A ball starts in the right arm's cup. The right arm must load it into the small basket of a passive see-saw launcher and move its cup away. The left arm, holding a mallet, must strike the lever so that the ball is flung up into free flight, and the right arm must catch it in its cup. The right arm then loads the ball into the basket a second time and clears away, and the left arm launches it again. In the end the ball must come to rest inside an open box that slides back and forth on a rail, while the box is moving. The left arm's mallet must never touch the ball. Phases, in order: physical_loading: the ball rests in the launcher's basket for 0.1 s without interruption. During that time the ball touches the lever (the lever link, basket included) and does not touch the right cup, and the lever is near horizontal (|q| < 0.12 rad). In the lever's frame (origin on the hinge axis, x along the beam toward the pad side, z normal to the beam), the ball centre is within 0.021 m horizontally of the basket centre (x, y) = (-0.12, 0) and between 0.024 m and 0.044 m above the hinge plane (the basket floor is at 0.012 m, so a resting ball sits at 0.030 m). The ball also moves at less than 0.08 m/s relative to the lever's centre-of-mass velocity. This is recorded once. After that, the right cup's tool frame must be more than 0.16 m away from the clearance point (0, 0, 0.18) (the ball need not still be in the basket at that moment).; first_launch: the left mallet (any part of panda-0's tool link) touches the lever or its pad; the first such contact in this phase is recorded. After that, the ball has touched nothing for more than 0.04 s while its centre is higher than z = 0.20 m.; right_catch: the ball drops into the right cup from free flight and stays there. Measured in the cup's tool frame, its centre crosses downward through the plane 0.073 m above the cup floor (wall height 0.055 m + radius), within 0.052 m (half width - radius) of the cup centre along both x and y, after the ball has touched nothing for at least 0.025 s. After that crossing the ball must stay retained in the cup for 0.18 s without interruption. Retained means: its centre is at least 0.45 x radius inside the inner walls (|x|, |y| < 0.0619 m in the tool frame) and between 0.014 m and 0.0528 m above the cup floor; it has touched the cup within the last 25 ms; and it moves at less than 0.09 m/s relative to the cup (the cup's rigid-body velocity at the ball's position).; reload_and_clear: the same as physical_loading, counted again only within this phase. The ball rests in the basket for 0.1 s without interruption: it touches the lever and not the right cup, |q| < 0.12 rad, its centre is within 0.021 m of the basket centre and 0.024-0.044 m above the hinge plane in the lever frame, and its speed relative to the lever is < 0.08 m/s. After that, the right cup's tool frame must be more than 0.16 m from (0, 0, 0.18).; second_launch: the same as first_launch, counted again only within this phase: the left mallet touches the lever or its pad, and after that the ball has touched nothing for more than 0.04 s while its centre is higher than z = 0.20 m.; moving_receptacle_retention: the ball is inside the moving box, and the box moves along its rail faster than 0.02 m/s, for 0.7 s without interruption. Inside means: in the box's frame the ball centre is at least 0.45 x radius inside the inner walls (|x|, |y| < 0.0669 m from the box centre) and between 0.014 m and 0.0578 m above the box floor; the ball has touched the box within the last 25 ms; and it moves at less than 0.09 m/s relative to the box. This completes the task. Goal geometry: Clearance point (0, 0, 0.18): in physical_loading and reload_and_clear the right cup's tool frame must finally be more than 0.16 m from it. Launch height: in first_launch and second_launch the ball centre must be above z = 0.20 m.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where the task has succeeded (every phase in order) or failed (a failure event, a forbidden contact, a safety-limit violation, an object out of bounds, or the task's horizon of 25 s of simulated time, 2500 control steps), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
